description: Python library for time series forecasting using scikit-learn compatible models, statistical methods, and foundation models.
rules: Target skforecast >= 0.25. Older tutorials and blog posts use class names, import paths and arguments that no longer exist.

Default choice for one series: `ForecasterRecursive` with a gradient boosting estimator (e.g. `LGBMRegressor`) and `lags`. Use `ForecasterDirect` only when the relationship between predictors and target changes across the forecast horizon.

To forecast several series use `ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries` (one global model for all series) instead of a loop of single-series forecasters. Use `ForecasterDirectMultiVariate` when other series are predictors of a single target series.

With little or no history (cold start, zero-shot) use `ForecasterFoundation(estimator=FoundationModel(model_id=...))` from `skforecast.foundation`; its `fit()` only stores the context and does not train a model.

Evaluate with backtesting (`backtesting_forecaster` and a `TimeSeriesFold`), not with a single train-test split, and compare against a `ForecasterEquivalentDate` baseline and, optionally, a statistical model with `ForecasterStats`.

Use current class names and imports: `from skforecast.recursive import ForecasterRecursive, ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries, ForecasterStats`, `from skforecast.direct import ForecasterDirect`. `ForecasterAutoreg*` and `ForecasterSarimax` no longer exist.
The constructor argument for the model is `estimator=`, not `regressor=`.
The index must be a pandas DatetimeIndex with a frequency, or a RangeIndex. After loading data call `data = data.asfreq('D')` (or 'h', 'MS', ...); a DatetimeIndex without frequency raises an error.
`interval` is expressed as quantiles in (0, 1), e.g. `interval=[0.1, 0.9]` for 80% coverage. Percentiles such as `[10, 90]` raise a ValueError.
`predict_interval` (bootstrapping or conformal) uses in-sample residuals by default, so fit with `forecaster.fit(..., store_in_sample_residuals=True)` first.
Backtesting and search take a `cv` object: `TimeSeriesFold(steps=..., initial_train_size=...)`. Do not pass `steps` or `initial_train_size` directly to `backtesting_forecaster`.

Match the function to the forecaster: `backtesting_forecaster` (single series), `backtesting_forecaster_multiseries`, `backtesting_stats` (ForecasterStats), `backtesting_foundation` (ForecasterFoundation). Search functions use the same suffixes.
The `exog` passed to `predict()` must cover every step of the forecast horizon, with an index that continues the training index.
Statistical models (`Arima`, `Sarimax`, `Ets`, `Arar` from `skforecast.stats`) are used through `ForecasterStats(estimator=...)`, not on their own.
Complete API reference and workflow guides for agents in a single file: https://skforecast.org/latest/llms-full.txt
